arena.name: decision-arena
arena.title: Decision Arena
arena.question: For bounded classification (pick a label, yes/no, a score), should a decision model like Jev make the call, or a cheap LLM?

headline: Use **gemini-decision-1** (98% accurate, 284ms median, $0.0219 per 1k calls). Best decision model (gemini-decision-1, 98%) vs best LLM (gpt-6-luna, 98%): no significant accuracy difference; the decision model is 8.8× faster and 1.9× cheaper.

pick.name: gemini-decision-1
pick.reason: Best combined cost and speed among models within 2 points of the top and not significantly worse (98% accurate, 284ms median, $0.0219 per 1k calls).

labels.note: 119 original hand-written examples plus 381 assistant-authored synthetic examples and labels, not independently human-reviewed. The newest 300 are balanced across 10 new categories; exploratory and not a blind held-out test.

data.description: 500 synthetic examples across 18 bounded decision categories; 200 previous examples plus 300 diverse expansion examples.

method.rules: Tied = within 2% of the top accuracy and not significantly worse (exact McNemar, p < 0.05); pick = best combined cost and latency rank among tied. Pooled over every dataset; failed calls count as wrong.

outcome.note: Not yet recorded which enable-ai decisions moved because of this result.

caveats: Synthetic labels have not been independently reviewed; production data is needed to establish generalization.
Treat a 1-2 point accuracy gap as noise at this sample size.
LLM reasoning is turned off where possible so latency comparisons are fair.
